body:
A board task can name a design, and the agent working it turns the design into working frontend code with few translation errors. This is the one part of Design that is task work. Depends on feature:9d778f6e03dea799 for `design:<id>`, and on a design to build from (feature:7c9cdfad16609a44, feature:aff58e018ae80474).

## Asked for

- A core requirement: translating a design to Lustre is easy for agents and doesn't introduce errors.
- Agents can access a design, refer to it and read it while working tasks.
- Designs are reference material on which agents base the frontend code.

## Decided

- **A design is reference material, not the source of truth for the code.** Agents write the code; Solace does not regenerate it. A design can go stale as soon as a feature adds a button or text, and a translation layer could overwrite existing UI.
- **Generating code directly stays an ideal for later**, if it ever proves safe.
- **The result is ordinary code.** A normal task says, for example, "build this screen from design:<id>". The code goes through the store and type check, and is recorded and reviewed like any other change.
- **Hand-editing the code is allowed.** With no generated code, there is nothing for an edit to fall out of step with, so the earlier question of refusing hand edits no longer applies.

## Suggested (cursory, not prescriptive)

- A run's brief tells the agent a named design exists and how to read it.
- A written mapping from each element type and property to Lustre gives agents one way to translate a design and makes errors rarer. Whether a guide is enough or Solace should give more help is for the investigation to say.

## Open

- How the reviewer checks that the built screen matches the design.
- What happens for a project that doesn't use Lustre, such as a Rust project. It could still design and preview, but this feature's help is aimed at Lustre.

## Not in this feature

Dropped along with code generation as the source of truth: generated view modules that nobody edits, typed action parameters, a generated theme module, and checks that flag generated code drifting from the design. Also left out: links from tasks to single elements.
title: design: build from a design
